title: Greek yogurt dough pizza
summary: A two ingredient yogurt and flour base spread straight into a baking dish, sauced, topped and baked in one go. Around 42 g of protein for 490 calories, with no dough to roll.

time.note: Bake 30 to 40 minutes depending how crisp you want the top.

nutrition_per_serving.note: The whole dish, which is how the source gives it. Figured with wholemeal flour - a white or gluten free flour drops the fibre to about 2 g and takes a few grams off the protein.

ingredients.note: Half the base by weight. It has to be thick - a runny yogurt gives you a batter too loose to hold its edge in the dish.

ingredients.qty: 60 g (the video used a gluten free flour)
ingredients.note: Any flour works here. The base is spread rather than stretched, so there is no gluten network to develop and nothing lost by going gluten free.
Any cooked protein does the same job - the swap table offers chicken, paneer, bacon and prawns.
Go light. The sauce, the mozzarella and the ham are all salty before you add any.

steps: Stir the yogurt and flour together until there is no dry flour left. At 150 g of yogurt to 60 g of flour this stays a thick spreadable paste rather than a dough you could roll, which is exactly why it goes into a dish instead of onto a tray.
Spread it into a small baking dish in an even layer, about a centimetre deep, pushing it right into the corners.
Spread the pizza sauce over the base, then scatter on the mozzarella and the ham.
Bake 30 to 40 minutes, until the top is browned and bubbling. Thirty minutes leaves it soft, forty gives you the crisp edges.
Eat it straight out of the dish with a fork. This is a deep soft base, not a slice you pick up.
tips: The one genuine swap for the Greek yogurt is thick plain yogurt strained for 20 minutes in a cloth. Unstrained curd holds too much water and the base never sets.
Push the paste properly into the corners. Wherever it is thin the sauce soaks straight through and that patch stays wet.
Any cooked protein works in place of the ham. Leftover roast chicken, paneer, bacon or cooked prawns all sit well on this - add prawns only for the last ten minutes so they do not turn rubbery.
It reheats better than it keeps. Give it ten minutes back in a hot oven rather than the microwave, which turns the base rubbery.
health_notes: The protein comes off three things rather than one: roughly 16 g from the yogurt, 10 g from the mozzarella and 9 g from the ham. The flour is nearly all of the carbohydrate, about 42 g of the 56, so this is the carb-heaviest recipe in here despite the protein.

source.title: Simple Homemade Healthy One Dish Pizza
source.adapted: Ingredients and the bake are from the video description, which gives no method at all. Every step here comes from the video: the yogurt and flour go into a baking dish as a spreadable paste rather than a rolled dough, and the finished thing is eaten out of the dish with a fork. Mushrooms are in the original list and are deliberately left out - Sartaj may be allergic, and mushroom is on the avoid list in preferences.json. Alternative proteins are added at his request as a one-way swap rule rather than extra ingredient lines. Nutrition is recalculated rather than copied: the stated 50 g of protein and 71 g of carbohydrate are each well above what these quantities give, though the 9 g of fat matches.
